name: LiteSpeed Cache
storage_notes: Every setting is a separate wp_options row named litespeed.conf.<id> (Root::name() builds 'litespeed.' + lowercase class + '.' + id; src/root.cls.php:563). Array values are JSON-encoded by Conf::_maybe_encode (src/root.cls.php:668). litespeed.conf.hash is a random 32-char secret, not a settings checksum; litespeed.conf._version is the installed schema version. Defaults come from data/const.default.json and class defaults, so many rows do not exist until configured. Cache/optimized files live under wp-content/litespeed (LITESPEED_STATIC_DIR, litespeed-cache.php:67).

settings.summary: Random 32-character security key generated on install and used for ESI HMAC/vary hashing. It is explicitly not settable and is skipped by Conf::update(). Never write it.
Internal configuration/version marker used by upgrade routines. Read-only.
Master page-cache switch. 0 off, 1 on; multisite also uses 2 (inherit network admin setting). Changing it purges all caches.
Cache private pages for logged-in users.
Enable separate mobile cache; user-agent rules are in cache-mobile_rules.
Enable browser cache headers; TTL is cache-ttl_browser.
Cache REST API responses according to cache-ttl_rest.
Public page TTL in seconds. Default 604800; UI recommends minimum 30.
Front-page TTL in seconds. Default 604800.
URLs excluded from cache. Array items are normalized to relative paths; changing it purges listed URLs.
Cookie names/patterns that bypass cache.
User-agent strings that bypass cache.
Query-string parameters ignored when matching cache entries.
URLs forced to be cached even if they would normally be excluded.
Purge the whole cache when a post is published/updated instead of selected ancestors.
Purge all caches after plugin upgrade.
Minify CSS.
Combine CSS files (CCS must be configured when enabled).
Generate and use Unique CSS; requires QUIC.cloud service quota.
Minify JavaScript.
Combine JavaScript files.
JavaScript defer mode; multi-switch 0/1/2 (off / deferred / delayed).
Minify HTML output.
Add font-display support to optimized CSS.
Enable native lazy loading for images/iframes.
Image replacement format; multi-switch 0/1/2 (off / WebP / AVIF). AVIF is a paid QUIC.cloud feature.
Enable LiteSpeed object cache. Related credentials are object-kind, object-host, object-port, object-user, object-pswd and object-db_id.
Enable the built-in crawler. Related options include crawler-sitemap, crawler-load_limit and crawler-crawl_interval.
Debug logging switch; multi-switch 0/1/2 (off / on / admin IP only).
Advanced debug detail switch used when debug logging is enabled.

actions.name: save_settings
actions.summary: Canonical settings write path: validates IDs, casts types, updates per-setting options, applies purge rules, updates cron and syncs config files.

actions.name: update_conf
actions.summary: Lower-level equivalent used by save_conf; calls Conf::update() per id then purge/file/cron side effects.

actions.name: get_setting
actions.summary: Read an effective setting, including defaults, constants, filters and multisite overrides.

params.id: string setting id without litespeed.conf. prefix

actions.name: purge_all
actions.summary: Purge LSCache, CSS/JS, local resources, object cache and OPcache; also Cloudflare if configured.

actions.name: purge_post
actions.summary: Purge cache entries related to one post ID.

actions.name: purge_posttype
actions.summary: Purge all cache entries for a post type.

actions.name: purge_all_lscache
actions.summary: Purge only the web-server page cache, leaving CSS/JS/object caches.

objects.storage: Filesystem wp-content/litespeed (LITESPEED_STATIC_DIR) plus LiteSpeed web-server cache entries
objects.summary: Page cache, optimized CSS/JS, CCSS/UCSS, image optimization placeholders and crawler data.
objects.crud_notes: There is no supported file-level CRUD. List/inspect via Purge and Crawler APIs; invalidate with purge_all, purge_url, purge_post or purge_posttype. Never delete files directly.

objects.summary: All plugin configuration; each setting is its own row rather than one serialized array.
objects.crud_notes: Read effective values with Conf::conf(). Write with API::save_conf()/Conf::update_confs() so validation, type casting, purge rules and .litespeed_conf file sync run. Raw update_option writes skip all of that.

detection.active_check: defined('LSCWP_V') or class_exists('LiteSpeed\Core'); plugin basename LSCWP_BASENAME = litespeed-cache/litespeed-cache.php

pro_notes: There is no separate LiteSpeed Cache Pro plugin. QUIC.cloud-dependent features (UCSS, image optimization, CDN) require an external QUIC.cloud account and service quota; AVIF output is explicitly a paid QUIC.cloud feature (tpl/img_optm/settings.media_webp.tpl.php:31). Cloud quotas/provisioning were not verified in this source analysis.
gotchas: litespeed.conf.hash is a random secret generated once (src/base.cls.php:873), not a checksum of settings; Conf::update() refuses it (src/conf.cls.php:721). Writing the other options does not require recomputing the hash and you must never overwrite/delete it.
Raw update_option('litespeed.conf.x', ...) skips type casting, validation, automatic purge and Activation::update_files() sync. Use API::save_conf() or Conf::update_confs().
Array settings are JSON-encoded in the option row by Conf::_maybe_encode() (src/root.cls.php:668); read through Conf::conf(), which decodes them.
Many option rows do not exist until first saved. Read with Conf::conf() (applies data/const.default.json defaults) instead of get_option() with a hardcoded default.
cache, debug, optm-js_defer and img_optm-webp are multi-switch values (0/1/2), not plain booleans; see src/base.cls.php:635.
TTL options are seconds, not minutes/hours; cache-ttl_pub defaults to 604800 and the UI warns below 30 seconds.
Multisite uses cache=2 to mean inherit the network setting; shared object-cache flushes require network authority.
Settings changes can trigger purge-all or per-URL purges inside update_confs(); expect cache warm-up after writes.
WP-CLI is available: wp litespeed-purge all|url|post_id|... (cli/purge.cls.php:68).
